Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor

Class JvmBuildTools

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor.JvmBuildTools
All Implemented Interfaces:
TextEditorExtension
public final class JvmBuildTools extends Object implements TextEditorExtension
The bundled "JVM Build Tools" extension: compiles, runs and debug-checks the current document with the real JDK toolchain, filed under the Java/Kotlin category next to JavaDevTools.

Compile / run shell out to the running JDK's own javac and to the JDK 11+ single-file source launcher, so a document works whether or not it was ever saved: the current text is staged into a fresh temp directory and built there, never touching the user's file. Debug is a crash-analysis run: assertions are enabled (-ea), the output is scanned for the exception heading and the first stack frame that lands in this file, and the status line reports "Debug: <exception> at Foo.java:<line>" with the full trace kept in the output console. (An interactive breakpoint debugger is a separate future feature; this is the honest in-editor subset.)

Kotlin actions drive kotlinc/kotlin from PATH; when the compiler is not installed the action degrades to a clear status message and starts no process.

Processes run on a virtual thread and the result is delivered back on the EDT, so the editor never blocks; a package-private JvmBuildTools.Runner seam keeps every action headless-testable with a synchronous fake. Every run, success included, writes a block to the editor's south OutputConsole (through the FILE_IO-gated EditorContext.showOutput capability) so the console always reflects the latest build — the document itself is never written to, and a legacy // ---- <tool> output ---- comment block left in a document by earlier builds is stripped automatically (WRITE) on the next action. Progress and exit codes always land on the status line.
